title: Sorting out problems
goal: Return things, ask for a refund, deal with customer care and the police, and settle a dispute calmly — and report exactly what everyone told you.
intro:
A wrong order, a phone that dies after a week, a refund that never arrives, a wallet gone missing, an auto driver who overcharged you: this unit is for the days when things go wrong. You'll learn to explain the problem, insist politely, and find a compromise.

The grammar is **reported speech in full**: 'he said that…', 'she asked whether…', and above all 'they told me to…' — the sentences you need when you're repeating to a manager what his staff promised you.

grammar.title: Reporting what people said and asked
grammar.body:
Unit 20 introduced ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ…. When you're sorting out a problem you report all the time: 'the shop said…', 'the man on the phone asked whether…'. Here is the full picture.

**1. Two ways to report a statement.** After **ਕਿ**, Punjabi can keep the speaker's **own words** (the most common way in speech) or shift them to your point of view:
own words: ਉਸ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ **ਮੈਂ** ਕੱਲ੍ਹ **ਭੇਜਾਂਗਾ** — lit. 'he said that I will send it tomorrow'
shifted: ਉਸ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ **ਉਹ** ਕੱਲ੍ਹ **ਭੇਜੇਗਾ** — 'he said that he would send it tomorrow'
Both mean the same. Either way, the **tense does not move back** as in English: 'will' stays -ਗਾ, 'is' stays ਹੈ: ਉਸ ਨੇ ਦੱਸਿਆ ਕਿ ਪੈਕਟ ਰਸਤੇ ਵਿੱਚ **ਹੈ** 'she said the package **was** on its way'.

**2. The verbs.** ਕਹਿਣਾ 'say' (ਕਿਹਾ), ਦੱਸਣਾ 'tell, inform' (ਦੱਸਿਆ), ਪੁੱਛਣਾ 'ask a question' (ਪੁੱਛਿਆ), ਮੰਨਣਾ 'admit' (ਮੰਨਿਆ). All follow the ਨੇ rule in the past. The person told or asked takes **ਨੂੰ**: ਉਸ ਨੇ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਦੱਸਿਆ.

**3. Questions** keep their question word: ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੇ ਪੁੱਛਿਆ ਕਿ ਮੈਂ ਆਰਡਰ **ਕਦੋਂ** ਕੀਤਾ ਸੀ. For a yes/no question ('whether'), put **ਕੀ** after ਕਿ: ਪੁੱਛਿਆ ਕਿ **ਕੀ** ਮੇਰੇ ਕੋਲ ਸਬੂਤ ਹੈ.

**4. Chatty reporting.** In conversation people drop ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ and use **ਕਹਿੰਦਾ / ਕਹਿੰਦੀ / ਕਹਿੰਦੇ** ('he goes…') or **ਅਖੇ** ('he says…, supposedly'). ਅਖੇ comes with a raised eyebrow — perfect for complaining: ਅਖੇ ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਤੱਕ ਆ ਜਾਊ! 'It'll be there by tomorrow, he says!'

**5. 'You told me…'** — the pluperfect ਕਿਹਾ ਸੀ / ਦੱਸਿਆ ਸੀ is how you hold people to their word: ਤੁਸੀਂ ਕਿਹਾ ਸੀ ਕਿ… 'you (had) said that…'.

The trap: ਪੁੱਛਣਾ is only for questions. 'He asked me to wait' is not ਪੁੱਛਿਆ — see the next note.

grammar.title: Reporting requests and orders: 'told me to…'
grammar.body:
To report a request, an instruction or a piece of advice, there are two patterns.

**1. ਨੂੰ + oblique infinitive + ਲਈ + ਕਹਿਣਾ.** The infinitive loses its final -ਆ: ਕਰਨਾ → **ਕਰਨ**, ਆਉਣਾ → **ਆਉਣ**, ਰਹਿਣਾ → **ਰਹਿਣ**, ਰੱਖਣਾ → **ਰੱਖਣ**.
ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੇ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਉਡੀਕ **ਕਰਨ ਲਈ** ਕਿਹਾ — 'they told me to wait'.
For 'not to', put **ਨਾ** before the infinitive: ਮੈਨੂੰ ਚਾਹ **ਨਾ ਪੀਣ ਲਈ** ਕਿਹਾ 'told me not to drink tea'. (In casual speech you'll also hear ਨੂੰ instead of ਲਈ: ਆਉਣ ਨੂੰ ਕਿਹਾ.)

**2. ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ + subjunctive** (or the original command):
ਪੁਲਿਸ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ ਮੈਂ ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਥਾਣੇ **ਆਵਾਂ** — 'the police said I should come to the station tomorrow'
ਪੁਲਿਸ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਥਾਣੇ **ਆਓ** — 'the police said: come to the station tomorrow'

**ਪੁੱਛਣਾ or ਕਹਿਣਾ?** English 'ask' does two jobs. Asking a **question** is ਪੁੱਛਣਾ; asking someone **to do something** is ਕਹਿਣਾ (formally ਬੇਨਤੀ ਕਰਨਾ): ਮੈਂ ਉਸ ਨੂੰ ਰੁਕਣ ਲਈ **ਕਿਹਾ** 'I asked him to stop' — never ਪੁੱਛਿਆ.

**Holding people to it**: ਤੁਸੀਂ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਬਿੱਲ ਰੱਖਣ ਲਈ ਕਿਹਾ ਸੀ, ਮੈਂ ਰੱਖਿਆ — 'you told me to keep the bill, and I did'. Calmly repeating what you were told is the strongest move in any dispute.

culture:
Many Indian shops display the sign **ਵਿਕਿਆ ਹੋਇਆ ਮਾਲ ਵਾਪਸ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੋਵੇਗਾ** 'goods once sold will not be taken back' — but most will **exchange** an item, especially if you're polite, have the bill and come back quickly. Refunds are easier with big chains and online orders, where the battle moves to customer care: be patient, note the complaint number, and ask for a supervisor (ਸੀਨੀਅਰ / ਮੈਨੇਜਰ) if you get nowhere.

The style that works is **calm and persistent**: ਜੀ and ਭਾਜੀ in every sentence, no shouting, and a precise account of who told you what and when (ਤੁਸੀਂ ਕਿਹਾ ਸੀ…). Shouting makes people lose face and dig in; a joke often opens the way to a ਸਮਝੌਤਾ. Haggling over a settlement — 'half and half?' — is perfectly normal.

For a lost or stolen phone, get the SIM blocked first, then file a police report (Indian states let you do it online) — insurers and the phone company will ask for it. Phone scams are common: no bank or company will ever ask for your OTP, and ਠੱਗ 'conman' is a word you'll hear a lot in the news.

tip.title: Returns: ਵਾਪਸ ਕਰਨਾ and ਵਾਪਸ ਹੋਣਾ
tip.body:
- **ਵਾਪਸ ਕਰਨਾ** 'to return, give back' — you do it: ਮੈਂ ਪੈਕਟ ਵਾਪਸ **ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤਾ**.
- **ਵਾਪਸ ਹੋਣਾ** 'to be refunded' — it happens: ਪੈਸੇ ਵਾਪਸ **ਹੋ ਗਏ**.
- In the past, ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤਾ agrees with the thing returned: ਜੁੱਤੀ ਵਾਪਸ ਕਰ **ਦਿੱਤੀ**.
tip.pattern: thing + ਵਾਪਸ ਕਰਨਾ  ·  ਪੈਸੇ + ਵਾਪਸ ਹੋਣਾ

lessons.title: What they told me

tip.title: He said that…: ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ, ਦੱਸਿਆ ਕਿ
tip.body:
- After **ਕਿ** you can keep the speaker's own words: ਉਸ ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ **ਮੈਂ** ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਭੇਜਾਂਗਾ 'he said he'd send it tomorrow'.
- The tense doesn't move back as in English: 'will' stays **-ਗਾ**.
- Venting? Use **ਅਖੇ** or **ਕਹਿੰਦੇ** ('they go…') instead of ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ.
tip.pattern: X ਨੇ ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ + their own words

lessons.title: They told me to wait

tip.title: Told me to…: ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਕਿਹਾ
tip.body:
- Instructions: **ਨੂੰ + verb-ਣ/-ਨ + ਲਈ ਕਿਹਾ**: ਮੈਨੂੰ ਕੱਲ੍ਹ **ਆਉਣ ਲਈ** ਕਿਹਾ 'told me to come tomorrow'. 'Not to' = **ਨਾ** before it.
- Or ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ + subjunctive: ਕਿਹਾ ਕਿ ਮੈਂ ਆਰਾਮ **ਕਰਾਂ**.
- 'Ask someone to do' is **ਕਹਿਣਾ**, never ਪੁੱਛਣਾ (that's only for questions).

tip.title: They asked whether…: ਪੁੱਛਿਆ ਕਿ ਕੀ…
tip.body:
- Reported questions keep their question word: ਪੁੱਛਿਆ ਕਿ ਫ਼ੋਨ **ਕਿੱਥੇ** ਗੁਆਚਿਆ.
- Yes/no questions ('whether') add **ਕੀ** after ਕਿ: ਪੁੱਛਿਆ ਕਿ **ਕੀ** ਮੇਰੇ ਕੋਲ ਬਿੱਲ ਹੈ.
- The person asked takes **ਨੂੰ**: ਉਸ ਨੇ **ਮੈਨੂੰ** ਪੁੱਛਿਆ.

lessons.title: Scams and blame

tip.title: Cheated: ਮੇਰੇ ਨਾਲ਼ ਧੋਖਾ ਹੋਇਆ
tip.body:
- Bad things happen **ਨਾਲ਼** 'with' you: ਮੇਰੇ **ਨਾਲ਼** ਧੋਖਾ ਹੋਇਆ 'I've been cheated'.
- Or name who did it: ਉਸ ਨੇ ਮੈਨੂੰ **ਠੱਗ ਲਿਆ** 'he ripped me off' (ਨੇ for the doer, ਨੂੰ for the victim).
- Blame: ਕਿਸ ਦਾ **ਦੋਸ਼** ਹੈ? · ਕੌਣ **ਜ਼ਿੰਮੇਵਾਰ** ਹੈ?
tip.pattern: X ਨਾਲ਼ ਧੋਖਾ ਹੋਇਆ  ·  X ਨੇ Y ਨੂੰ ਠੱਗ ਲਿਆ

tip.title: Settling it calmly
tip.body:
- Suggest with **ਆਪਾਂ** + subjunctive: ਆਪਾਂ ਬੈਠ ਕੇ ਗੱਲ **ਕਰੀਏ** 'let's sit and talk'; ਅੱਧਾ ਅੱਧਾ ਕਰ **ਲਈਏ**? 'shall we split it?'
- 'How about if…?' = **ਜੇ … ਤਾਂ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਰਹੇਗਾ?**
- Keep the temperature down: ਆਰਾਮ ਨਾਲ਼ ਗੱਲ ਕਰਦੇ ਹਾਂ, ਗੁੱਸਾ ਨਾ ਕਰੋ.
